# Corpus Mining — Bradford Hatcher, *The Book of Changes: Yijing, Word by Word*, Volumes One & Two (Hermetica.info, Nucla CO, 2009; Vol 1 ISBN 978-0-9824191-1-3, Vol 2 ISBN 978-0-9824191-2-0)

Source: `/mnt/agents/upload/Yijing1-2.pdf` → `/tmp/yijing12.txt`. **Identification**: two-volume literal/word-by-word Yijing translation with matrix translation, structural study ("Dimensions"), history, and full glossary. This PDF = both volumes concatenated. Hatcher is an independent scholar-translator (not academic sinology; he is explicitly anti-"modernist"); his **structural/dimensional apparatus is the most complete formal state-space description in this corpus** — vol 2 "The Dimensions" is essentially an operator algebra over 6-bit diagrams.

Volume One contents: Introduction (78 Diagrams, Preface, Notes, Problems with Academia, **Structure of the Diagrams**, Methods of Divination); Part One: Zhouyi + first four Wings, simple translation; **Part Two: Xiao Gua, The Small Symbols (the 2+4+8 small diagrams with full correspondence lists, pp. 443–485)**; Part Three: History; Part Four: Glossary (Characters, Phrases, Not in Glossary, Most Common Words, Pinyin).
Volume Two contents: Matrix Translation (all 64 gua with Chinese text); **Part Four: The Dimensions** (Correlative Thought; Gua Ming names; **Gua Bian changes**; Gua Xu sequences; Qian Gua inverse pairs; Pang Tong Gua opposite pairs; Jiao Gua reverse pairs; **Hu Gua nuclear diagrams**; Shi Er Di Zhi twelve branches; Gua Xiang images; Ban Xiang half-images; San Cai three powers; Yao Wei line positions; Yao De line characteristics; Figures 1–40); Glossary; Index Keys.

Conventions: `O`=Rou/yin line (0), `I`=Gang/yang line (1); `W R H Y` = four emblems; trigram digits 0–7 and hexagram numbers 00–63 are **Xian Tian binary** (yin=0; yang in line position n (bottom=1) = 2^(n-1); top line = one's place). Received chapter numbers 01–64 = Hou Tian (King Wen). Page numbers cited are the books' printed pages (vol 1 and vol 2 sequences).

---

## A. TEXTUAL STRATA & METHOD
- Eight "False" claims dismantled (vol 1 p. 1–2), incl.: the Zhouyi is NOT 5000 years old; Yin-Yang force philosophy is anachronistic to the Zhouyi; the Ten Wings are NOT a reliable guide to original thought; **no evidence that trigrams existed when the Zhouyi was written (they appear Spring & Autumn period)** — though Hatcher argues the *text construction* implies early trigram-image use (vol 2 p. 22).
- Layer abbreviations (vol 1 p. 50): `.M` Gua Ming name; `.0` Gua Ci (Zhouyi hexagram text); `.1–.6` Yao Ci (Zhouyi line texts); `.T` Tuan Zhuan (Wings 1–2); `.X/.x` Da Xiang / Xiao Xiang (Wings 3–4); `.xc` Xi Ci Zhuan / Da Zhuan (Wings 5–6); `.wy` Wen Yan (Wing 7); `.sg` Shuo Gua (Wing 8); `.xg` Xu Gua (Wing 9); `.zg` Za Gua (Wing 10); `.m` Mawangdui variants. Zhouyi dated 1100–800 BCE; Yijing = Zhouyi + Ten Wings; Yixue = the whole tradition.
- Zhouyi vocabulary <900 characters; first four Wings add <300 (vol 1, intro p. ~19).
- Hatcher's parsimony rule: "Start with the concrete … Then seek to understand it as magic and myth, then as a metaphor or analogy, then as an abstract ethical philosophy" (vol 1 p. 21).

## B. FORMULAIC DIVINATION PHRASES (syntax/morphemes)
- **Yuan Heng Li Zhen 元亨利貞** (vol 1 pp. 21–23): NOT four parallel ideas; Hatcher: "The greatest rewards are the result of sustained hard work." Yuan = superlative (first/principal/great/supreme; Wings wrongly gloss as Da 'great'); Heng = offering→fulfillment (Janus word: xiang sacrifice ↔ pervaded by spirit/success); Li = earned advantage (knife-of-harvest graph); Zhen = determination/resolve/test/verification (Janus: divination-determination ↔ persistence). Later mapped to four seasons "but this was not at all the case in the Zhouyi."
- Prognostication valence set in use: Ji 吉 Promising; Xiong 凶 Unfortunate; Hui 悔 Regret; Lin 吝 Embarrassment; Wu Jiu 無咎 No blame ("nothing wrong"…"no harm done", vol 1 p. ~24); plus "No blame, no praise" (wu yu wu yu). Statistical line-place distribution: Ji most frequent at lines 5 & 2, rarest line 3; Xiong most at lines 6 & 3, rarest 5 & 4 (vol 2 p. 26 — supports Xi Ci II.9).
- Zhi-nomenclature (vol 2 pp. 12–13): pre-Wing divination citations named lines as "Gua X **zhi** Gua Y" = "X goes to / results in Y" (e.g. "Da Zhuang zhi Tai" = the line of Da Zhuang that changes into Tai, i.e. line 4) — destination built into the name; later simplified to "1st 9, 6 2nd…" losing the Ben→Zhi thought.

## C. PRIMITIVES — STRUCTURE OF THE DIAGRAMS (vol 1 pp. 43–44)
- Four casting numbers: 6 = Old/Stressed Yin (changes to yang/7), 7 = young yang (stable), 8 = young yin (stable), 9 = Old/Stressed Yang (changes to yin/8). Written: Six = X, Eight = broken, Seven = solid, Nine = 0.
- Hexagram built bottom→top (1st → Top). **Ben Gua** (Original/Root) → change moving lines → **Zhi Gua** (Resultant/Approached). Yao Ci = interpolation in meaning between Ben and Zhi (Hatcher's central thesis, with Hellmut Wilhelm).
- Multi-line method: "Transitional Hexagrams" (Mondo Secter's term): change lines one at a time from lowest up, reading only the lowest changing line's text at each intermediate gua.
- Trigram halves = **Ban Xiang** (Half Images): bottom three = **Zhen Gua**, top three = **Hui Gua** (vol 1 p. 44).
- Coin method: one side = 2, other = 3; sum of three coins ∈ {6,7,8,9}. Chinese preference: 4-character side = 2; Hatcher uses heads = 2.
- **Xian Tian binary numbering** (vol 2 p. 15): yin=0, yang = 32,16,8,4,2,1 by position (bottom→top); hexagrams are "the six-digit binary numbers from decimal 00 thru 63. … No table is needed to look up these numbers: they are numbers."
- **Seventy-Eight Diagrams = 2 + 4 + 8 + 64** (vol 1, front matter): the complete formal inventory.
- Eight change-system types known to history (vol 2 p. 12): "1) Evolution or derivation (yao into xiang into Ba Gua into Gua …); 2) Combination (e.g. two Ba Gua make up a Gua); 3) Sequence (gua xu); 4) Cycle (gua qi, omitted here); 5) Substitution (ba gong); 6) Transposition (jiao gua); 7) Permutation (shi er di zhi); 8) Interpolation (zhi gua / Gua Bian)." History: Cai Jingjun (140–90), Meng Xi (90–40), Jing Fang (77–37), Jiao Yanshou's Yilin (each gua → all 63 others; 2^12=4096 possibilities); minimum system = 448 possibilities (64 static + 384 single-line).
- Xian Tian Ba Gong (vol 2 pp. 15–16): the 8×8 binary grid ("Eight Houses of the Primal Heaven") on which **"every single structural dimension of the Yijing plots out with mathematical symmetry"** — the master coordinate system. Fig. 1 grid (rows=upper trigram 0–7, cols=lower 0–7, cells = "binary,chapter" pairs) fully transcribed in vol 2 p. 32.

## D. GENERATION / SCALE THEORY (Xiao Gua, "Introduction to Scales", vol 1 pp. 443–447)
- Scales = divisions of a continuous spectrum that survive if they "cover a spectrum … and resonate (ying) within our beings" (p. 444). Color/sound examples: scale-of-2 = warm/cool; octaves by frequency doubling.
- **Scale of One**: Wu / Wu Ji / Tai Ji (Tai Yi in Han) — Zhou Dunyi's Taijitu (p. 445).
- **Scale of Two** = Er Yao (Two Lines) / Er Chi / Liang Yi: "concerned with matched complements and not with paired antagonists" (p. 445).
- **Scale of Three**: two forms — Synchronic/Spatial (San Cai: Heaven–Humanity–Earth; an equally weighted mediator between two contrasts) and Diachronic/Temporal (past Wang / present Jin / future Lai; "this kind of triplicity, which of course concerns Change, is at the heart of the way the Book of Changes is used", p. 446). Trigram line positions as temporal triplicity: bottom = Beginning (Zhen goes; Xun ready to go), middle = While Going (Kan concentrates/integrates; Li appreciates/differentiates), top = After Going (Gen stops; Dui savors satisfaction).
- **Scale of Four**: universal quadruplicity; cross-cultural lists accrue but no perfect translation between systems (p. 446).
- Ba Gua gender from San Wei: "where there are two masters (gang) and one subject (rou), this is a daughter; with one master and two subjects, a son … The Three Places represent the ages of the children: lowest is eldest, highest is youngest" (vol 2 p. 24, San Cai section, citing the Wings).
- Da Ba Gua (Great Trigrams): Tai Yin / Tai Yang emblems occupying the three two-line pairs (1-2, 3-4, 5-6) of a hexagram (vol 2 p. 24, Fig. 13).

## F. THE DIMENSIONS (vol 2, Part Four, pp. 8–31) — the operator/rule layer

### F1. Correlative Thought (pp. 4–7)
Dimensions are invoked as evidence only where they explain the words of the text; each has a discoverable stratum (Zhouyi vs Wings vs Yiweishu/Han vs post-Han).

### F2. Gua Ming — Hexagram Names (pp. 8–11)
Names introduced as standalone words (embedded in syntax only at Gua 10, 12, 13, 52). Zhouyi authors used **dichotomy** to define names against structurally resonant partners, most often along the Inverse (Qian Gua) and Opposite (Pang Tong Gua) axes: e.g. 41/42 Decreasing/Increasing; 51/52 motion/rest; 57/58 mental/emotional (inverse); 01/02, 11/12, 29/30, 51/57, 52/58 (opposite). Note: 51, 52, 57, 58 are paired on BOTH axes — "two different dimensional axes" (p. 11). Purpose: "internal resolution of paradox as a path to wisdom."

### F3. Gua Bian — Hexagram Changes (pp. 12–13)
- **Zhi Gua rule**: every single-changing-line Yao Ci is an interpolation between Ben Gua (root) and Zhi Gua (resultant); Hatcher lists 146 clear Zhi Gua-referencing lines (01.1; 02.3; 03.2; … 64.6 — full list on p. 13).
- **Fan Yao (Reverse-Line) Pairs** — Hatcher's coined term: "two Yao Ci form a resonant pair when they have a reciprocal Zhi Gua relationship, that is, they meet on a path while moving in opposite directions, with each one coming from the other's destination." They share vocabulary, cross-references, subjects, grammatical tone. 50 pairs listed (01.6↔43.6; 02.3↔15.3; 03.3↔63.3; 05.3↔60.3; … 56.6↔62.6 — full list p. 13). [Operationally: A.line-i→B and B.line-j→A.]

### F4. Gua Xu — Hexagram Sequences (pp. 14–15)
- Received sequence = Hou Tian Xu / Wen Wang Xu. **Algorithm: "Every even numbered Gua is the Inverse of the Gua which precedes it, except in cases where a Gua is its own Inverse — then the preceding Gua is an Opposite."** → 32 structurally meaningful pairs "placed in random sequence" (p. 14).
- Mawangdui order (168 BCE tomb) demonstrates awareness of trigrams as components (upper-trigram families — see Moore doc App. 1).
- **Xian Tian Xu** (Shao Yong, 1011–1077): the 64 gua as binary 00–63 — "the proper sequence, regardless of the history." Read forward = accumulation of yang in increasingly fundamental positions ("the launching of the dragon … Left Hand Path"); backward = accumulation of yin's adaptability ("the slaying of the dragon … Right Hand Path") — "not mutually exclusive paths but a paradox of wisdom" (p. 15).
- Xian Tian Ba Gong 8×8 grid: every structural dimension plots symmetrically; the Middle Path (Fen, equal yin/yang balance) lights up from Separating(12) to Interplay(11); also fractional sequences (sevenths, ninths).

### F5. Qian Gua — Inverse Pairs (p. 15–16)
28 pairs, line-sequence reversed (figure turned upside down). Also called Fu (overturned) / Dian (inverted). The 8 symmetrical (self-inverse) gua are excluded (1,2,27,28,29,30,61,62 — Fig. 27). Full pair list (p. 16): 23-24, 08-07, 20-19, 16-15, 35-36, 45-46, 12-11, 52-51, 39-40, 53-54, 56-55, 31-32, 33-34, 04-03, 59-60, 64-63, 47-48, 06-05, 18-17, 57-58, 50-49, 44-43, 42-41, 21-22, 25-26, 37-38, 13-14, 10-09. Semantic effect: complements "at different times on a cycle (syzygy)"; inverting "will also often contrast essentialist and existential points of view."

### F6. Pang Tong Gua — Opposite Pairs (p. 17)
32 pairs, all six lines changed (also called Bian, transformed). "In the Xian Tian binary sequence all pair numbers add to 63, i.e. they are mathematical complements." "A Gua's opposite is its least likely Zhi Gua" (single-line distance maximal). In Shao Yong's circle they sit opposite. Full list: 02-01, 23-43, 08-14, 20-34, 16-09, 35-05, 45-26, 12-11, 15-10, 52-58, 39-38, 53-54, 62-61, 56-60, 31-41, 33-19, 07-13, 04-49, 29-30, 59-55, 40-37, 64-63, 47-22, 06-36, 46-25, 18-17, 48-21, 57-51, 32-42, 50-03, 28-27, 44-24.

### F7. Jiao Gua — Reverse Pairs (p. 18)
28 pairs, same two trigrams in swapped (upper↔lower) positions. The 8 Chong Gua (doubled trigrams) are their own Jiao Gua. First explicit in Han Yiweishu; Yu Fan called them Fan Gua. Use: "1) the objective applicability of more intimate subjective experience (inner to outer) or 2) the internalization of an objective experience … Logically speaking, Reverse is a Converse, a reversal of subject and predicate." Full list: 23-15, 08-07, 20-46, 16-24, 35-36, 45-19, 12-11, 39-04, 53-18, 62-27, 56-22, 31-41, 33-26, 59-48, 40-03, 64-63, 47-60, 06-05, 32-42, 50-37, 28-61, 44-09, 21-55, 17-54, 25-34, 49-38, 13-14, 10-43.

### F8. Hu Gua — Nuclear Diagrams (pp. 18–19) — THE NUCLEAR RULE
- **Rule: lower Hu Ti (互體) = lines 2,3,4; upper Hu Ti = lines 3,4,5; combine → Hu Gua (nuclear hexagram).** Wang Yinglin quoting Zheng Xuan tradition: "sets of the second, third and fourth lines and sets of the third, fourth and fifth lines mingle together but each set separately forms a trigram … 'one hexagram contains four trigrams'" (Zheng Xuan 127–200 emulating Fei Zhi 50 BCE–10 CE; practice "has existed since Mr. Zuo [4th cent. BCE]"; systematic use develops among Yiweishu, perhaps as early as Jing Fang 77–37 BCE; Hu Gua proper = post-Han).
- **Only 16 gua can be nuclei; each is nucleus of exactly 4 others; 02 and 63 [Kun-all-yin and Qian-all-yang… binary 00 and 63] are their own Hu Gua.** "akin to a latent idea or matrix, a potential or tendency, like a seed within a fruit."
- **Second nuclear hexagrams**: only four — the binary third-points 0/3, 1/3, 2/3, 3/3 (= gua 02, 23/24 family… = 02, 24, 43, 01 effectively).
- Full nucleus→domain table (p. 19): 02: 02,23,24,27 · 23: 08,20,03,42 · 39: 16,35,51,21 · 53: 45,12,17,25 · 40: 15,52,36,22 · 64: 39,53,63,37 · 28: 62,56,55,30 · 44: 31,33,49,13 · 24: 07,04,19,41 · 27: 19,59,60,61 · 63: 40,64,54,38 · 37: 47,06,58,10 · 54: 46,18,11,26 · 38: 48,57,05,09 · 43: 32,50,34,14 · 01: 28,44,43,01.

### F9. Shi Er Di Zhi — Twelve Branches / Sovereign Gua (p. 20)
- 12-Moon sovereign-gua system attributed to Meng Xi (90–40 BCE) per Yu Fan; **"Internalizing the 12 Branches" (branches paired to the 12 lines of Qian & Kun) attributed to Jing Fang (77–37 BCE)** — the Najia-adjacent line-assignment attestation.
- Permutation rule: from a base gua change line 1, then line 2 … to top (= its Opposite), then repeat bottom-up to return. Base pairs = Chong Gua + opposites; families: Kun-Qian (the famous one), Kan-Li, Gen-Dui, Xun-Zhen; "No Family" gua excluded.
- **12 Moons table (complete)**:
  | moon | month | gua | branch | zodiac | seasons |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | Feb | 11 Tai | Zi Rat | Aries | Spring Begins; The Rain |
  | 2 | Mar | 34 Da Zhuang | Chou Ox | Taurus | Insects Awaken; Vernal Equinox |
  | 3 | Apr | 43 Guai | Yin Tiger | Gemini | Clear & Bright; Grain Rain |
  | 4 | May | 01 Qian | Mao Hare | Cancer | Summer Begins; Grain Buds |
  | 5 | Jun | 44 Gou | Chen Dragon | Leo | Grain in Ear; Summer Solstice |
  | 6 | Jul | 33 Dun | Si Serpent | Virgo | Slight Heat; Great Heat |
  | 7 | Aug | 12 Pi | Wu Horse | Libra | Autumn Begins; Heat Stops |
  | 8 | Sep | 20 Guan | Wei Goat | Scorpio | White Dews; Autumnal Equinox |
  | 9 | Oct | 23 Bo | Shen Monkey | Sagittarius | Cold Dews; Hoarfrost Falls |
  | 10 | Nov | 00(02) Kun | You Cock | Capricorn | Winter Begins; Light Snow |
  | 11 | Dec | 24 Fu | Xu Dog | Aquarius | Heavy Snow; Winter Solstice |
  | 12 | Jan | 19 Lin | Hai Boar | Pisces | Slight Cold; Great Cold |
  (Yang grows bottom-up Feb→May, peaks Qian, yin returns Jun→Nov, trough Kun — the canonical 12 tidal/sovereign hexagram cycle.)

### F10. Gua Xiang — Hexagram Images (pp. 20–22)
Whole-figure pictographs used by Zhouyi authors: 02 = open furrow; 23 = too-tall mountain; 20 = observation tower; 62 = bird in flight; 50 = ding cauldron; 44 = undermining; 24 = seed deep in earth / road home; 27 = open mouth; 61 = window into private space; 34 = horns; 43 = too-tall lake/about to burst; 28 = overloaded; 01 = whole and full. Ba Gua Xiang (combined natural images): sun over earth (35) / sun under earth (36); heaven-earth positions (11, 12); fire-water positions (63, 64).

### F11. Ban Xiang — Half Images; Zhen/Hui semantics (pp. 22–23)
- Lower (Zhen) = subjective, the Who, "coming to"; upper (Hui) = objective, the How, "going through" (Lai Wang). Zhen = "converging forces of the situation, the coming together of its vectors, one's personal momentum … bases, motives, needs, hopes and potentials: the past arriving at presence … persistence, commitment or focus (Heng, Gua 32)". Hui = "diverging possibilities … choices or alternatives and subsequent directions … skills, tools and raw materials … the present arriving at the new" (etymologically hui = many-hearted, regret for choices forgone).
- The Xian Tian Ba Gong grid cross-referenced by lower×upper = "a catalog of attitudes … sixty-four unique permutations, or different relationships of Subjective to Objective."
- Nuclear places nuance: Line 1 already left behind in lower Hu Ti (commitment begun); Line 6 not yet touched by upper Hu Ti (consequences inconclusive) — mid-course core of the situation lives in the nuclear structure.

### F12. San Cai — Three Powers (p. 24)
Shuo Gua §2 (transcribed with pinyin): "In ancient times the wise ones composed the Yi … in establishing Heaven's way, spoken of yin along with yang; in establishing Earth's way, spoken of flexibility along with firmness; in establishing Humanity's way, spoken of compassion along with right conduct. Connecting (these) Three Powers, and then doubling them, resulted in the Yi's six pictures and (its) completed Gua." Probably a Wing dimension. Spatial/synchronic scale: Earth below, Heaven above, Humanity the fertile border between: "Heaven begins at our feet … The Earth ends at the tops of our heads." Heaven = day/night, sun/moon (mental); Humanity = movement/stillness (social); Earth = hardness/softness, dryness/moisture (natural, not inert).

### F13. Yao Wei — Six Line Positions (pp. 25–27)
- Zhouyi-internal evidence: "heads are not seen in Line One, feet are not seen in Line Six"; the gua maps time (bottom = first stages, top = outcome/past it); body, family, social, class, political analogies.
- Xi Ci Zhuan II.9 (transcribed in full with pinyin): "The first line is difficult to know, the top line is easy to know: (these are) the roots and branch tips … Line two (is) related to line four, similar in merit but different in position … Line two is frequently praised; line four is frequently cautioned … Line three is related to line five … line three is frequently adverse; line five is frequently effective. The honored and the mean are as ranks. One's flexibility is perilous, one's firmness overcomes the perverse."
- Shchutskii's summary (quoted): line 1 = very beginning, not yet typical; 2 = apogee of INTERNAL development; 3 = crisis, transition internal→external; 4 = beginning of EXTERNAL appearance (favored by proximity to 5); 5 = maximum external exposure; 6 = completion/over-development, "either loses its typicality or turns into its opposite."
- **Line-place correspondence lists (Hatcher's, from Zhouyi usage)**:
  - Body: L1 feet/toes/sandals; hooves, tail; ground, grass, roots · L2 calves/legs/knees · L3 thighs/hips/loins/waist/rump · L4 [torso — truncated] · L5 [upper body] · L6 [head] [partially truncated in extraction; L1–L3 verbatim].
  - People: L1 newcomer/apprentice/innocent/youth; common people · L2 assistant/subordinate/servant/mother/maiden/woman in home · L3 lower official/subordinate/worker/journeyman/local leader · L4 chief minister/officer/duke/son/empowered delegate · L5 sovereign/authority/executor/leader/husband/father; man at work · L6 sage/climber/refugee/retiree/extremist/diehard/elder/advisor.
  - Situations: L1 seeds planted, prepare basics, many unknowns · L2 time for Zhen (persistence/commitment/focus); situations broaden · L3 complexity, details, many responsibilities, little mastery yet · L4 familiarity if not mastery; effects of diligence begin to appear · L5 the time bears its fruit; moderation suited to mastery and nobility; "the merit shows" · L6 "the best time to know when to stop, reflect, wrap up, integrate and enjoy."
  - Structural places: L1 bottom of lower trigram · L2 center of lower trigram, bottom of lower Hu Ti · L3 top of lower trigram, bottom of upper Hu Ti, center of lower Hu Ti · L4 bottom of upper trigram, center of upper Hu Ti, top of lower Hu Ti · L5 center of upper trigram, top of upper Hu Ti · L6 top of upper trigram.
  - **Binary values: yang in position n = 2^(n−1): L1=32, L2=16, L3=8, L4=4, L5=2, L6=1.**

### F14. Yao De — Line Characteristics (pp. 27–29) — the Wing/Yiweishu rule-set
NOTE: Rou/Gang terms "do not appear in the Zhouyi"; Yang absent, Yin only as 'shade/shadow' — these pairs first appear in the Ten Wings.
- **Zhong 中 Centrality**: line 2 or 5 (middle of lower/upper trigram) = central, in balance → statistically better auspice.
- **Dang 當 Appropriateness**: rou correct in even positions (2,4,6), gang in odd (1,3,5); Wang Bi: not applicable to lines 1 & 6. Gua 63 Ji Ji = completely Dang; Gua 64 Wei Ji = completely Bu Dang.
- **Zheng 正 Correctness**: subset of Dang, reserved for 9-in-5th.
- **Ying 應 Resonance**: corresponding places in lower/upper trigrams (pairs 1-4, 2-5, 3-6) resonate when one is rou and the other gang. Wang Bi: "Resonance provides an image of shared purpose." The 8 gua made of opposite trigram pairs are fully Ying; the 8 Chong (doubled) gua are completely Bu Ying (no correspondence).
- **Fen 分 Even Apportionment**: equal rou/gang count in a gua; balance assumed auspicious.
- **Bi 比 Holding Together**: adjacent rou+gang lines; more auspicious if both Dang; most auspicious pair = 6-4th / 9-5th. Lower of pair "Carries/Receives (Cheng)" the upper; upper "Rides/Avails of (Cheng)" the lower.
- **Lin 鄰 Neighborhood**: converging dimensions create a 'neighborhood' from which helpers/friends/gifts come in the texts.
- **Sheng Jiang Yao 升降爻 Rising/Falling**: gang lines rise/go; rou lines fall/sink/return — within the gua-as-time-map.
- **Ruling Lines (Governing Rulers in bold / Constituting rulers plain) — full Yiweishu table**: 01: **5**; 02: **2**; 03: 1,**5**; 04: **2**,6; 05: **5**; 06: **5**; 07: **2**,5; 08: **5**; 09: 4,**5**; 10: 3,**5**; 11: **2**,5; 12: **2**,5; 13: **2**,5; 14: **5**; 15: **3**; 16: **4**; 17: 1,**5**; 18: **5**; 19: 1,2; 20: 5,6; 21: **5**; 22: 2,6; 23: **6**; 24: **1**; 25: 1,**5**; 26: 5,6; 27: 5,6; 28: 2,4; 29: 2,5; 30: 2,5; 31: 4,5; 32: **2**; 33: 1,2,5; 34: **4**; 35: **5**; 36: 2,5,6; 37: 2,5; 38: 2,5; 39: **5**; 40: 2,5; 41: 3,5,6; 42: 1,2,4,5; 43: 5,6; 44: 1,2,5; 46: 1,5; 47: 2,5; 48: **5**; 49: **5**; 50: 5,6; 51: **1**; 52: **6**; 53: 2,5; 54: 3,5,6; 55: **5**; 56: **5**; 57: 1,4,5; 58: 2,3,5,6; 59: 2,4,5; 60: 3,4,5; 61: **5**; 62: 2,5; 63: **2**; 64: **5**. ## G. RULES EXTRACTED (numbered)
1. R-H1 Casting: three coins (2/3 per side) → 6/7/8/9 per line, built bottom→top; 6,9 moving.
2. R-H2 Change: moving yang(9)→yin; moving yin(6)→yang → Zhi Gua. Ben→Zhi interpolation generates Yao Ci meaning.
3. R-H3 Fan Yao pairing: reciprocal Zhi-Gua line pairs.
4. R-H4 Combination: 2 trigrams → hexagram (Zhen below = subjective/past-momentum; Hui above = objective/future-options).
5. R-H5 Nuclear extraction: lines 2-3-4 and 3-4-5 → Hu Ti → Hu Gua; 16 nuclei, 4 domains each; 4 second-order nuclei.
6. R-H6 Inverse (Qian Gua): reverse line order; 28 pairs; 8 self-inverse.
7. R-H7 Opposite (Pang Tong): flip all 6 lines; 32 pairs; binary complements summing to 63.
8. R-H8 Reverse (Jiao Gua): swap upper/lower trigrams; 28 pairs; 8 Chong Gua self-reverse.
9. R-H9 Hou Tian sequence algorithm: even gua = inverse of predecessor, else opposite.
10. R-H10 Xian Tian numbering: yin=0, yang=2^(n-1); sequence 00–63; read both directions.
11. R-H11 12-Branch permutation: change lines 1→6 successively then back (12-step cycle through opposite); sovereign-gua/moon assignment table (F9).
12. R-H12 Yao De set: Zhong, Dang, Zheng, Ying, Fen, Bi (cheng riding/carrying), Lin, Sheng Jiang, Ruling Lines (table above).
13. R-H13 Scale generation: 1→2→3→4→8→64 (Scale of One: Wu Ji→Tai Ji; yao→si xiang→ba gua→gua by line doubling); temporal triplicity beginning/while-going/after-going mapped to trigram line positions.
14. R-H14 Trigram gender/seniority from odd-line-out (position = birth order).
15. R-H15 Transitional hexagrams: multi-moving-line readings change one line at a time from lowest.
16. R-H16 Yuan-Heng-Li-Zhen = Four Qualities (si de) mapped to Si Xiang (yuan→Shao Yang/spring, heng→Tai Yang/summer, li→Shao Yin/autumn, zhen→Tai Yin/winter) — later layer, not Zhouyi.

## H. CANDIDATE DIMENSION ATTRIBUTION (project dims)
- Er Yao / Rou-Gang key-word fields: Hatcher explicitly maps Rou=**space, spatial**, Gang=**time, temporal** (key words u) → Space & Evolution pair at the 1-bit level; but as state primitives they are Being. Recommend: the *glyph* (0/1) = Being; the *polarity semantics* split Space (Rou) / Evolution (Gang) per Hatcher's own list.
- Si Xiang: explicitly seasonal/time-of-day (Evolution/when) + directional (Movement/where) + material-state Solid/Liquid/Gas/Plasma (Being/state) + dimension row (Length/Time/Breadth/Depth → Design/Space). The four emblems are the first genuine 4-state register — strong candidate for a 2-bit dimensional cell.
- Ba Gua nature images + family/body/animal = Being; Hou Tian compass + winds + gates = Movement; Xian Tian binary + Ba Gong grid + pair operators = Design; seasons/times/lunar/sovereign cycles = Evolution; Zhen/Hui inner-outer + nuclear cores + resonance (Ying) = Space (container/resonance — Hatcher: Hu Gua "contextual matrix within which the change occurs").
- Yao Wei line-places (roots/branch-tips, internal apogee→external exposure arc) = Evolution (a when-arc) instantiated in Design positions.
- Yao De relations (Zhong/Dang/Ying/Bi) = Design (structural form constraints).
